name: itamarst/cambridge-dining

Data manually pulled from opentable.com/state-of-industry, not scraped/API. Jupyter notebook does the analysis.
why_useful: OpenTable seated-diners is explicitly named in gap #6 as a public consumer/leisure-spend indicator; this repo shows a working method to pull/parse it, even though scope (one city) is narrow.

name: itshyunseunglee/jeju-card-analysis
what_it_holds: Jeju Island (South Korea) regional card-spending dataset 2017-2018, used to analyze where/when a cafe would do well by area and time.
why_useful: A worked example of a national card-spend dataset by region/time outside the US/EU, structurally analogous to what a BBVA/CaixaBank/Norges Bank card panel would look like (regional card spend by merchant category); could serve as an APAC/Korea travel-adjacent consumer-spend proxy, though geography (Jeju, a tourist island) and vintage (2017-18) are dated and not KTO/travel-specific.
themes: Public consumer-spend panels: Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker (Affinity card spend), ONS card spending, Bank of England CHAPS, BBVA/CaixaBank research open data, Banco de Portugal SIBS, Norges Bank card data

name: ooi-darren/project-007-global-consumer-spending
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, 10-commit repo with a 182-country annual consumer-spending panel (data/processed/master_consumer_spending.csv), 2013-2023, built from World Bank household consumption expenditure/GDP/population/urbanisation/internet-penetration data, World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, and OECD 12-category (COICOP) household spending shares for 36 countries (category_spending_shares_oecd.csv), plus a latest_year_snapshot.csv and a UN M49 region-mapping file. No isolated travel/tourism/accommodation spend category confirmed; annual frequency only.
why_useful: Marginal: annual, country-level, non-point-in-time macro consumption data that mostly duplicates World Bank/OECD/Eurostat series the team likely already has cheaper access to (and does not isolate travel spend); the COICOP category-share file for 36 countries could be a minor cross-check for discretionary-spend share trends by country, but nothing here is finer-grained or more current than existing holdings.
size_hint: Small (~182 rows x few dozen columns for the main panel; ~36 rows for category shares)
last_activity: 10 commits total; recent given repo is a 2026-era portfolio project, exact date not confirmed
duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with existing Eurostat/BEA PCE/OECD consumer-confidence holdings; adds little
